families.reason: Both cards individually checked. They ask which closed decimal interval contains a rational number; 317132 gives 5/9 in [0.5,0.6], and 353058 gives 7/11 in [0.6,0.7]. The generator preserves closed endpoints and the independent oracle checks displayed bounds.

All four cards individually checked. 317223 asks which interval contains √53; 49 < 53 < 64 gives [7,8], option 4. 337311: √73→[8,9], option 1. 352483 (OGE 2024): √60→[7,8], option 2. 425018 (OGE 2022): √57→[7,8], option 2. The generator preserves square-root bracketing by consecutive integers and the oracle squares the visible radicand and displayed options.

Both cards individually checked: choose which radical belongs to the closed interval [6,7] or [7,8]. Independent squaring gives √42 for [6,7] and √61 for [7,8]; this matches the generator's visible interval and root options.
Card 369728 asks which rational number is in the closed segment [3,4]; 68/19 is the only value in that interval (answer 3). The generated structure preserves closed membership and shuffled options.

Card 311420 is attributed to a 2013 historical diagnostic and asks which listed decimal lies between 1/6 and 1/4. The implemented generator instead asks for an arbitrary decimal strictly between integer endpoints. This is a structure/goal mismatch and the historical card is not enough to approve it.
Card 461837 asks which consecutive integers bracket 131/12; exact division gives 10 < 131/12 < 11 (answer 1). This matches the generator's signed-rational floor structure.

The original diagrams for 384400 (√85, point A), 322293 (√53, point A), and duplicate 449733 (same as 384400) were visually checked. They show four labeled points against integer divisions and ask which point is the radical; independent bounds identify the marked location. The generated analogue uses a saved exact radical model and pixel-audited number line.

474133 confirms a current four-point number-line question (58/7 corresponds to C; direct image inspected). 311380 is a 2013 historical variant with a different fractional subdivision scale (0, 1/6, 1/3, …), which the current integer-tick generator does not model. Hold until the family is split or fractional ticks are implemented and audited.

The cards give each point's coordinate in the condition and ask which point corresponds to a target decimal; 370464 has −0.267, −0.112, 0.041, 0.271, target 0.271→D. The current generated condition omits coordinates of the other points and relies on approximate positions, so it does not preserve the source's visible information.

Direct visual inspection confirms the point-A diagram with integer ticks 2 and 3 and choices √5, √7, √11, √14. Since A lies between 2 and 3 and nearer 2, squaring/bounding identifies √5 (answer 1). Generated tasks preserve the same point-to-radical structure and exact graph model.

317074 has a point between 0.5 and 0.6 on a tenths scale, with choices 10/23, 12/23, 13/23, 14/23; the answer is 13/23 (option 3). Historical 311392 uses a different fractional subdivision. Current renderer shows integer ticks only, so the point's rational coordinate is not recoverable from visible marks.
